title: Taylor Johnson-Cook state and postprocessing
objective: Add Johnson-Cook state update integration and Taylor postprocessing for final geometry and equivalent plastic strain.

plan_assets.asset_description: Phase E7 Johnson-Cook state output and Taylor postprocessing requirements.

scope: Use existing JohnsonCookMaterial and Johnson-Cook return mapping.
Track finite stress, temperature, and equivalent plastic strain in the Taylor runtime.
Add postprocessing for final length, mushroom radius, and equivalent plastic strain localization.
implementation_steps: Run GitNexus impact before editing existing Johnson-Cook symbols.
Integrate Johnson-Cook state update into the internal Taylor runtime.
Add state extraction for temperature and equivalent plastic strain.
deliverables: Johnson-Cook state integration in Taylor runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Johnson-Cook state update produces finite stress, temperature, and equivalent plastic strain.
Final length and mushroom-radius postprocessing is deterministic.
Johnson-Cook model behavior is unchanged unless a focused defect is proven.
risks: Johnson-Cook impact on existing tests is medium; mitigate by avoiding semantic edits and adding focused runtime integration tests.
completion_notes: Added init_taylor_runtime_jc, explicit_step_jc, extract_equivalent_plastic_strain, final_length, mushroom_radius to mechdsl.verify.benchmarks._taylor_runtime.
Per-element JC state (eqplas, temperature, pk2_stress) lives on ExplicitTaylorState.material_state; integrated via existing radial_return primitive — zero upstream JC drift.
extract_equivalent_plastic_strain returns a true copy (verified by mutate-and-check test).
final_length and mushroom_radius are bit-for-bit deterministic; mushroom_radius defines the radial center via reference impact-face coordinates so a uniform translation does not change the radius.

Gate C attempt 1 caught a calibration miss in the user-authored test_finite_johnson_cook_state_update (dt=1e-9 was an order of magnitude smaller than the 1mm-element wave-traversal time of ~200 ns, so no element saw the impact wave within the 10-step horizon). Recalibrated dt to 1e-8 (factor-20 subcritical); assertion preserved.
